calls.body: The Flames are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at keeping shots away. We’ll side with the Flames.

calls.head: McNabb and Theodore get the Backlund assignment
calls.body: At home, the Golden Knights keep sending McNabb and Theodore out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Craig has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Flames’ first line is Backlund, Farabee and Sharangovich.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: A natural hat trick for Stone
paras: Brett Howden struck first for the Golden Knights just 25 seconds into the game, and Jack Eichel made it 2-0 shorthanded midway through the first. Jake Middleton scored his first goal for Calgary shorthanded midway through the second to get the Flames on the board. Braeden Bowman stretched the lead to 3-1 on the power play 48 seconds later. The third period belonged to the Golden Knights: Mark Stone scored, Stone scored his second of the night, and Stone completed a natural hat trick on the power play to make it 6-1. Matt Coronato cut Vegas’ lead to 6-2 on the power play with less than two minutes left, but by then the game was long gone. There were two three-point nights: Eichel with a goal and two assists, and Ivan Barbashev with three assists.
The Golden Knights drove the play, and the scoreboard caught up. Carter Hart made 28 saves for the Knights, and Dustin Wolf allowed six goals on 33 shots.
Raphaël Lavoie and Middleton picked up ten-minute misconducts. The Golden Knights improved to 7-2-0, and the Flames dropped to 1-6-0.

items.text: Mark Stone tied William Karlsson for second on the Golden Knights’ all-time scoring list, with 407 points.
Jack Eichel passed Jonathan Marchessault for fourth on the Golden Knights’ all-time assists list, with 227.
Mitch Marner extended his point streak against Calgary to seven games.
Mitch Marner has a point in five straight games.
